> 'Nobody would prevent anyone from eating'

That isn't really the point though. Whenever there is progress the majority of people stop doing the 'old' thing in favour of the 'new' thing. column50: If you listen carefully to a vinyl record playback you can hear, very faintly, the start of a track at little before it actually starts. A 'pre-echo' that starts exactly one turn of the table before. \nThe master record is cut in a relatively soft material. Copper, I think. The force of cutting removes material from the groove but also compresses the remaining material somewhat. This distortion may spill over into the neighbor groove just cut one turn earlier. The neighbor groove is silent between tracks. So in this silence you may be able to hear a faint copy of the modulation one turn later. This ghost signal gets more volume the tighter you pack the groove spiral, which you may want to do tighter to obtain longer playing time.
